scope: Segment DL2 host-originated, separator-free, self-delimited ('!' ... '~') primary/secondary transaction dial-string segment carried in the Table Load Response (Data Block No. 2, Conditional) and the Phone Load Response (Required)
extractionEvidence: regression-artifact-validator/specifications/ATL105/docs/specs/extracted_text.txt lines 17207-17300 (Section 12.43), 9240-9345 (Section 11.7.2 Phone Load), 9090-9130 (Section 11.7.1.2 Data Block No. 2), 19367-19384, 20131-20160, 20888-20905, 20970-20986, 21175-21183 (Section 13.2 Elements 1, 27, 28, 66, 75, 82)

rules.title: Segment DL2 maximum length is 69 alphanumeric characters; originates at BUYPASS (Host); Data Type Indicator fixed '!' (field 1), End-of-Data Indicator fixed '~' (last field)
rules.note: 69 = '!' + Dial String Type + primary block (1+12+1+18+'A') + secondary block (1+12+1+18+'F') + '~', i.e. both blocks at maximum width.

rules.title: Dial String Type is fixed value 1; Primary Phone Number block (fields 3-7: Redial Count, Access Code [conditional], Pause Indicator [conditional, fixed 'B'], Phone Number, Dial String Terminator fixed 'A') is required

Secondary Phone Number block (fields 8-11) mirrors the Primary block's structure, terminated by a Dial String Terminator fixed 'F' (field 12); the secondary number is used only after all primary-number retry attempts are exhausted per the Asynchronous Communications Protocol Specifications error-recovery logic
rules.note: PROVISIONAL: the detailed error-recovery logic is defined in a separate 'Asynchronous Communications Protocol Specifications' document not available in this KB pass (SEGDL2-SME-001). In-spec evidence: Element 75 says 'Transaction dialing always begins with the primary Phone Number. The secondary Phone Number is used once attempts using the primary Phone Number are exhausted'; Element 82 bounds the redial count to 1-3.

rules.title: Segment DL2 fields are not separated by Field Separators; when a field is not populated (Access Code, Pause Indicator) the next field immediately follows
rules.note: Segment 100's empty-field separator rule does not apply. Parsing of the variable-length Access Code and Phone Number relies on 'B' and the terminators 'A'/'F' (SEGDL2-SME-004).

rules.title: If Access Code (Element 1) is not necessary, the dial string contains neither the Access Code nor the Pause Indicator (Element 66) that immediately follows it; the Access Code may itself contain one or more 'B' characters, each interpreted as a one-second pause
rules.note: Applies to both the primary and the secondary block. Pause Indicator valid value is 'B' only; a Hayes-command modem replaces 'B' with a comma when dialing.

rules.title: Redial Count (Element 82) is one digit with valid values 1-3 in both the primary and the secondary block

Phone Number (Element 75) is numeric, variable length up to 18 digits; Dial String Type (Element 28) is fixed '1' (transaction dial strings); Dial String Terminator (Element 27) is 'A' after the first dial string and 'F' after the second
Segment DL2 is Conditional in the Table Load Response (Data Block No. 2) and Required in the Phone Load Response, and is sent only on those two responses
rules.note: In the Table Load Response a Start-of-Data Block Indicator ')' precedes DL2 for dial connections but not for TCP/IP. The Phone Load Response field 1 framing is open under SEGDL2-SME-003.

rules.title: A Phone Load takes place only when the merchant profile load flag is PHON (set by a BUYPASS representative or automatically after a full load); when the flag is not set, the Downline Load Response contains only an error message block and a terminating block, so Segment DL2 must be absent
rules.note: The Phone Load Request (11.7.2.1) is '?' + Terminal Identifier + Load Type 'P' and carries no DL segment.
